notes.title: Future Roadmap and Steam Settings Update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

Today I made some little updates to the Steam settings for Little Fighter 2 Remastered:
[olist]
Achievements are now localized in Chinese  

[strike]Steam Remote Play is now enabled[/strike] <— some issues remain in Steam Remote Play and I will addressed them after the work on network play and controller support is completed.
[/olist]
Also, I’ve attached the current roadmap for LF2 Remastered below. While it hasn’t changed, I’m sharing it here for those who haven’t purchased the game but are curious about what’s planned (it’s also viewable in-game).

I’m continuing to work hard on bug fixes and exploring Steam’s matchmaking system. Stay tuned!
[hr][/hr]

Little Fighter 2 Remastered Roadmap

Here’s the planned roadmap for future updates, listed by priority. Items without a \[DLC] tag will be included in future updates for free once completed. If unexpected and unsolvable technical challenges arise, some features may be delayed or even canceled, but I’ll do my best to complete at least 70% of the plan.

• Network mode using Steam matchmaking: So players no longer need to enter IP addresses or set up port forwarding. 

• Cost-based VS mode: In this mode, each character has a cost value based on their strength. Teams share a total cost budget.

     • When a player is defeated, their character's cost is deducted from the team’s remaining budget.

     • If the budget hits zero, the team loses. 

• \[MUST DO] Support for gamepads. 

• Support Steam Big Picture Mode (under consideration). 

• \[DLC] Artbook: Includes full-resolution sprites, illustrations, and outline sketches. 

• \[DLC] Original Character Pack: Playable character using the original 2002 LF2 sprite. 

• \[DLC] Unlock All Content: Instantly unlock all stages and characters (all content can still be unlocked through gameplay; this DLC is just for those who want to show support). 

• \[MUST DO] Stage 6 with new characters: Note that the boss of Stage 6 will be extremely overpowered and won’t be available as a playable character for regular players. 

• \[DLC?] Workshop Support (under consideration): Might allow users to modify sprites and backgrounds more easily. 

• Remaster the sprite of the character Template. 

• ...Plus some old bugs to fix, and a few fan-requested features, such as the option to disable item drops or set a time limit in VS Mode. These fan requests might even be implemented before some of the features mentioned above!

notes.title: Working on an update to fix issues with input, stats, and Louis’s jump.
notes.notes:
Thank you so much for getting the game on Steam and reporting issues. I'm truly sorry about the bugs.

I'll be fixing the bug where Louis jumps too low, and the one where all characters share the same stats (like running speed). Yes, that’s definitely a bug... not a feature.

The next thing I’ll address is keyboard support. I’ll try to bring back Ctrl, Alt, Shift, and Enter, and using function keys F1-F9 instead of Shift + Number. Also working on a fix for the issue where input doesn't work when Caps Lock is on. However, support for F12 (screenshot) may take a bit more time.

I’ll try to fix the urgent issues mentioned above with an update in the next few days (along with some other bug fixes). F12 screenshot support may come later.


Regarding the lag issues, they generally fall into three main types:



(1) Network Play Lag:

Why does the game lag during online matches?

Please refer to this article: https://lf2.net/_/about_network_mode.html

The reason is that LF2 does not use rollback netcode. Because of this, any internet latency will be directly reflected in gameplay. This is due to the nature of how the game handles networking, not because of poor implementation.

That means delays from any of the following can cause lag: router hops, Wi-Fi stability, signal interference, ISP routing, data center distance, server load... even solar activity or a cat walking past your Wi-Fi router.



(2) Lag in Standalone Mode:

Some users report lag even in offline mode. This could be related to how the game engine (Pixi.js) manages textures and memory.

If you have browser windows open playing video, or if other applications are consuming a lot of memory, it may force the engine to frequently swap graphical assets in and out of memory, leading to stuttering.

Try closing unnecessary background apps or browser tabs to reduce this issue.



(3) Keyboard Input Delay:

Some players have reported input lag. Today, many people use Bluetooth keyboards, which typically have a delay of 30–80ms. While this usually doesn’t matter, expert players might notice the difference. If you're sensitive to this, a wired keyboard is recommended.

That said, there may still be room for optimization on my side. Especially to improve input handling under laggy conditions (as described in 1 and 2). I hope to address this in a future update.

Stay tuned — I'm working hard on the next update patch to improve the game. Thank you, as always, for your support!
